glosses: to clean up, to tidy up
to beat it, to clear off
passive of убира́ть (ubirátʹ)
приводить в порядок что-либо; производить уборку чего-либо

examples.text: Она покойно лежала, сложа у морды лапы, когда он входил в клеть, и, глядя на веник, понимала, что солдат пришел убираться.

Я видела, что эти люди терпели её как бы для чёрной работы, которую она иногда выполняла: куда-то звонила, что-то выясняла, доставала одним знакомым через других книги, кого-то с кем-то мирила, помогала убираться в квартире, и всё это делала ни за что, точнее, просто за то, что её терпят.

glosses: устар. наряжаться, украшаться
To make an area or a thing clean; to pick up a mess; to tidy.

examples.text: Rhos station had been cleaned up for the occasion, and its single platform was gay with flags.
Mr Mayor, you were elected in a campaign to clean up the city. When are you gonna start?
At the same time, it is pouring money into cleaning up the country.
Clean up your room.

glosses: To become clean, handsome, smart in appearance, e.g. for a special occasion, especially when it is out of character to be seen as such.

examples.text: He sure cleans up nice.

glosses: To make something less corrupt or unseemly.

examples.text: clean up one's act

Gays in Providence have suggested that the raid on the Club Baths was a political action. There is some belief that the newly re-elected Cianci administration wants to prove that it is "out to clean up the city." During the election campaign, the Cianci administration was attacked by opponents as being "soft on crime."

glosses: To make a large profit; to win by a large margin, or to win a large amount, especially in gambling. Also clean house.

examples.text: Man, he sure cleaned up last night at the blackjack table.
The investors cleaned up when the stock hit the roof last year.

And for Rodgers, who cleaned up with Celtic in Scotland, this was another significant addition to his CV, as his expert guidance of Leicester - who are in a strong position to finish in the Premier League's top four and face Chelsea again at Stamford Bridge on Tuesday - now has a tangible reward in the shape of the FA Cup.

glosses: To intervene in a fight between two players at low health and easily kill both of them or the winner.

examples.text: The key here is to stop third partying and start cleaning up. Running to the first bullets you hear will only guarantee one thing, a fight. […] Cleaning up means only swooping in for the free kills. Is a fight over? Does Octane has his hands in a deathbox? That is when you take the zipline and catch them with their pants down.

glosses: Misspelling of cleanup.
разг., груб. удаляться, уезжать, убегать, уходить откуда-либо или куда-либо

examples.text: Казакевич отменил задание, выплатил бригадиру отступные и велел убираться из Москвы.
Сергей понял, что пора убираться, пока Саня не оделся и не ввязался в драку.

glosses: перемещаться внутрь чего-либо

examples.text: Упоры стыковых замков, устанавливаемые на передаточной тележке и рельсовом пути стеллажного крана-штабелера, должны автоматически убираться после осуществления стыковки передаточной тележки и рельсовых путей кранов-штабелеров и автоматически возвращаться в исходное положение после расстыковки замков.

glosses: рег. помещаться

examples.text: Эти кроссовки не уберутся в сумку

glosses: To leave or escape.

examples.text: In case of fire, get out by the nearest exit.
You have to get out on a bull to succeed in a rodeo.

‘It is grim reading,’ he said. ‘I fear their end was cruel. Listen! We cannot get out. We cannot get out. They have taken the Bridge and second hall. Frár and Lóni and Náli fell there. Then there are four lines smeared so that I can only read went 5 days ago. The last lines run the pool is up to the wall at Westgate. The Watcher in the Water took Óin. We cannot get out. The end comes, and then drums, drums in the deep. I wonder what that means. The last thing written is in a trailing scrawl of elf-letters: they are coming. There is nothing more.’ Gandalf paused and stood in silent thought.

glosses: To come out of a situation; to escape a fate.

examples.text: Never take life seriously. Nobody gets out alive anyway.

glosses: To be released, especially from hospital or prison.

examples.text: He's been in prison for six months, but he gets out next week.

glosses: To remove one's money from an investment; to end an investment.

examples.text: I think copper prices will plummet this fall, so I'm getting out while I can.

glosses: To help (someone) leave.

examples.text: We must get the children out first.

glosses: To take (something) from its container or storage place, so as to use or display it.

examples.text: Get the playing cards out and we'll have a game of snap.
It's time to get the Christmas decorations out.

glosses: To leave the inside of a vehicle such as a car. (Note: for public transport, get off is more common.)

examples.text: I'll get out at the end of the road and walk from there.

glosses: To become known.

examples.text: Somehow the secret got out.
We have to act before that fact gets out on us.

glosses: To spend free time out of the house.

examples.text: You work too hard. You should get out more.

glosses: To publish or make available; to disseminate.

examples.text: The organization has just gotten their newsletter out.
This candidate is struggling to get her message out.

glosses: To say with difficulty.

examples.text: He could hardly get the words out for the tears.

glosses: To remove or eliminate (dirt or stains).

examples.text: This detergent will get most household stains out.

glosses: To end.

examples.text: School gets out in the afternoon.

glosses: Commanding a person to leave.

examples.text: Get out! I never want to see you in here again!

glosses: Indicating incredulity.

examples.text: "Giants in armour, sir. Hundred feet high. Three legs and a body like 'luminium, with a mighty great head in a hood, sir." "Get out!" said the lieutenant. "What confounded nonsense!".

glosses: Expressing disapproval or disgust, especially after a bad joke.

examples.text: Just get out.

glosses: 打掃，收拾
滾開
